name: harper
description: Offline, privacy-first grammar checker. Fast, open-source, Rust-powered
readmeExcerpt:
Harper

Harper is an English grammar checker designed to be _just right._ I created it after years of dealing with the shortcomings of the competition. Grammarly was too expensive and too overbearing. Its suggestions lacked context, and were often just plain _wrong_. Not to mention: it's a privacy nightmare. Everything you write with Grammarly is sent to their servers. Their privacy policy claims they don't sell the data, but that doesn't mean they don't use it to train large language models and god knows what else. Not only that, but the round-trip-time of the network request makes revising your work all the more tedious. LanguageTool is great, if you have gigabytes of RAM to spare and are willing to download the ~16GB n-gram dataset. Besides the memory requirements, I found LanguageTool too slow: it would take several seconds to lint even a moderate-size document. That's why I created Harper: it is the grammar checker that fits my needs. Not only does it take milliseconds to lint a document, take less than 1/50th of LanguageTool's memory footprint, but it is also completely private. Harper is even small enough to load via [WebAssembly.](https://writewithharper.com) ## Language Support Harper currently only supports English, but the core is extensible to support other languages, so we welcome contributions that allow for other language support. ## Performance Issues We consider long lint times bugs. If you encounter any significant performance issues, please create an issue on the topic. If you find a fix to any performance issue, we would appreciate the contribution. Just please make sure to read [our contribution guidelines first.](https://writewithharper.com/docs/contributors/introduction) ## Links - [Frequently Asked Questions](https://writewithharper.com/#faqs) - [Obsidian Documentation](https://writewithharper.com/docs/integrations/obsidian) - [`harper-ls` Documentation](https://writewithharper.com/docs/integrations/language-server) - Supported Editors' Documentation - [Visual Studio Code](https://writewithharper.com/docs/integrations/visual-studio-code) - [Neovim](https://writewithharper.com/docs/integrations/neovim) - [Helix](https://writewithharper.com/docs/integrations/helix) - [Emacs](https://writewithharper.com/docs/integrations/emacs) - [Zed](https://writewithharper.com/docs/integrations/zed) - [`harper.js` Documentation](https://writewithharper.com/docs/harperjs/introduction) - [Official Discord Server](https://discord.com/invite/JBqcAaKrzQ) ## Huge Thanks This project would not be possible without the hard work from those who [contribute](https://writewithharper.com/docs/contributors/introduction). Harper's logo was designed by [Lukas Werner](https://lukaswerner.com/).

Harper

Harper is an English grammar checker designed to be just right. I created it after years of dealing with the shortcomings of the competition.

Grammarly was too expensive and too overbearing. Its suggestions lacked context, and were often just plain wrong. Not to mention: it's a privacy nightmare. Everything you write with Grammarly is sent to their servers. Their privacy policy claims they don't sell the data, but that doesn't mean they don't use it to train large language models and god knows what else. Not only that, but the round-trip-time of the network request makes revising your work all the more tedious.

LanguageTool is great, if you have gigabytes of RAM to spare and are willing to download the ~16GB n-gram dataset. Besides the memory requirements, I found LanguageTool too slow: it would take several seconds to lint even a moderate-size document.

That's why I created Harper: it is the grammar checker that fits my needs. Not only does it take milliseconds to lint a document, take less than 1/50th of LanguageTool's memory footprint, but it is also completely private.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A lightning-fast, privacy-first grammar checker built in Rust for developers and writers.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Harper is a highly performant grammar and spell-checking engine designed to operate entirely offline, guaranteeing absolute user privacy. Written completely in Rust, it provides a significantly faster alternative to cloud-based tools like Grammarly, while demanding only a fraction of the memory footprint of local tools like LanguageTool. It is engineered to provide 'just right' suggestions, avoiding overly pedantic stylistic corrections in favor of meaningful, context-aware fixes. The core engine is highly versatile, compiling seamlessly to WebAssembly for browser use or running as a native language server in modern IDEs.
keyFeatures: Offline analysis: Processes all text locally on the user's machine to ensure sensitive data is never transmitted to the cloud.
Rust-powered performance: Delivers near-instantaneous grammar validation with an exceptionally low memory footprint.
WebAssembly compilation: Allows for seamless integration directly into web applications, text areas, and browser extensions.
Language server protocol: Integrates natively into modern code editors to provide developers with real-time feedback on documentation.
Nuanced rule set: Focuses on delivering contextually meaningful corrections while ignoring overly aggressive stylistic dictates.

useCases.title: Secure document drafting
useCases.description: Professionals handling sensitive corporate or legal documents can check grammar without exposing data to third-party servers.

useCases.title: Developer workflow integration
useCases.description: Software engineers can receive real-time spell checking for their code comments and documentation directly within their IDE.

useCases.title: Lightweight browser checking
useCases.description: Users can run a fast, local alternative to mainstream grammar extensions for everyday typing and email drafting.

useCases.title: Automated CI/CD validation
useCases.description: Teams can integrate the engine into their build pipelines to reliably lint markdown documentation before publishing.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Privacy-conscious writers, developers, and enterprises who require fast, reliable grammar checking without sacrificing data security.
